In high school here in Chicago, it was my nightmare subject—always bombing tests and dreading homework. I'd skip ahead to biology or art classes that actually excited me. Numbers and formulas make me zone out; I'd rather read novels, cook, or do yoga. Barely passed with Cs, and now I avoid it completely since I'm unemployed and free.","Do you ever get anxious when thinking about mathematics?":"Absolutely, math triggers my anxiety big time. Just seeing equations makes my heart race, palms sweat, and stomach churn—like reliving high school panic attacks. With my neurotic side, I overthink every step and fear messing up. Physics too, ugh. I breathe deep with yoga to calm down, but yeah, even casual thoughts stress me out.","Did you ever use AI to support your math learning in the last year? As an unemployed 19-year-old, it's handy for quick checks, but no miracle worker.","How would you explain, step by step, how to solve a second order algebraic equation?":"A second-order equation is ax² + bx + c = 0. Or factor: find p,q where p*q=ac, p+q=b, so (x+p)(x+q)=0. I always plug into formula, but double-check! I'd watch YouTube; biology data viz uses it, but I skip the math.","According to you, how can LLMs be used to innovate math learning in schools and universities?":"LLMs could revolutionize math ed! High openness to tech, but keep simple—no jargon overload."},"reasoning_summary":"Replies embody a casual, extraverted 19-year-old Chicago woman hating math (hat_subject), anxious (high neuroticism), basic high school knowledge, positive/open to AI/innovation, weaving in hobbies/life for authenticity in human mode."}
